message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $241 and own six properties. I hold four unmortgaged streets: ST CHARLES PLACE, STATES AVENUE, ST JAMES PLACE, and TENNESSEE AVENUE. WATER WORKS is also unmortgaged. NEW YORK AVENUE is mortgaged.

I also own MARVIN_GARDENS. The orange set is complete but I cannot build because NEW YORK AVENUE is mortgaged. I hold two of three pinks and lack Virginia. p2 has a dark blue monopoly with $165 cash, so they cannot build houses yet.

p3 has a light purple monopoly with hotels and owns Illinois and Pacific as singles. p4 holds a light blue hotel set, Virginia, three yellows, and the Short Line. Atlantic Avenue is unowned. The bank has 32 houses and 7 hotels.

Mortgaging all six properties would raise liquidity to $776. Unmortgaging New York Avenue would cost $110, leaving only $131 cash and worsening survival odds.

I cannot afford to build three houses on the orange set. I will avoid selling my pink properties or Marvin Gardens to p4, since that would complete their monopolies. The priority is survival and blocking p4 from inheriting Boardwalk if p2 goes bankrupt.

I am weighing trade offers. p4 could complete a yellow monopoly by acquiring Atlantic and Marvin, so I must never sell Marvin to them. If p4 also gains St Charles and States, they would own the entire pink set. p3 has brown hotels worth roughly $450 and $250, plus $731 cash.

p2 is vulnerable. With only $165 cash and no houses, they could go bankrupt if they land on a light blue hotel. I am weighing whether to trade with them to secure Indiana or help them survive so p4 cannot inherit their dark blue monopoly.

I am now considering selling Water Works to p3. That would give p3 a utility monopoly, but the cash would improve my survival buffer. Indiana, North Carolina, and railroads are not useful additions.

Selling Water Works to p3 would only add about $70 in cash, which is too small to change the game. p3 already owns Illinois and Pacific, so I cannot complete a red or green set with them. Trading with p4 is too risky because they have enough cash to finish monopolies.

I cannot buy Virginia from p4 to complete the pink set, since they will not sell a monopoly-completing property cheaply. Atlantic Avenue is unowned and unavailable. The current strategy remains survival, holding blockers, and avoiding mortgages or early builds. I am now considering a trade with p2 to help them survive bankruptcy while extracting value.

I rejected giving p2 cash, since that would let them build dark blue houses. I am now considering buying Park Place or Boardwalk from p2 to break their monopoly before they can develop it.

I realized p2 already owns both Park Place and Boardwalk unmortgaged, so their dark blue monopoly is complete. My earlier plan to buy those properties from them is no longer relevant.

I am now considering buying Park Place from p2 for $200. That would leave me with only $41 cash, which is too risky. If I succeed, p2 would keep Boardwalk and could not build houses. This would prevent p2 from developing the dark blue set and block p4 from inheriting a full monopoly if p2 goes bankrupt.

Mortgaging all six properties would raise cash to $776, allowing a $400 offer for Park Place. However, mortgaged properties stop paying rent, and the orange set is my main income source. This trade would sacrifice rent income to break the dark blue monopoly.

The orange set only yields about $28 in rent, and the pinks add roughly $10 each. Breaking the dark blue monopoly is the highest leverage defensive move available. If p2 survives and eventually builds houses, that set would kill everyone. If p2 goes bankrupt to p4, p4 inherits the full dark blue set plus light blue hotels and nearly complete yellows, which would be an instant loss for all players. The real threat is p4, not p2. I estimate p2 would demand $400 to $600 for Park Place because it is their only winning path.

I calculated the exact survival threshold. One light blue hotel costs $600, leaving me with $176 after mortgaging all six properties. Two hits would leave me bankrupt unless I can mortgage enough to cover both.

A $400 offer for Park Place would leave only $376 cash, which is still too low to survive a light blue hotel hit. I am now exploring alternative trades with p2 or p3, since p2 needs cash rather than properties and p3 has substantial funds.

I will not help p4. I am now considering proposing a trade to p2 for Park Place, but I must decide whether to act this turn or wait. The engine may ask again after p2 responds.

Proposing a trade consumes the action and the engine will ask again after the response. A $200 cash offer for Park Place would leave p2 with $365, still short of the $400 needed to build one house on each dark blue property.

I rejected the trade with p2. They would not sell Park Place for $200 because that would destroy their dark blue monopoly, and they are not in debt.

Option B is also unworkable. p2 has no cash shortage right now.

I am now considering selling Water Works to p3. If p3 owns both utilities, rent would be 10 times the dice roll, averaging about $70 per turn.

Selling Water Works to p3 would raise cash by only $100–$150, which is too small to justify the trade. It would also give p3 a utility monopoly and eliminate my own 4× dice rent income. I am now considering whether to mortgage properties immediately.

Mortgaging is ruled out because of the 10% interest penalty and the loss of rent income. Unmortgaging New York Avenue would cost $110 and leave only $131 cash, yet the engine lists no buildable properties, so building houses is impossible right now.

One house on the orange set would still leave me bankrupt if I unmortgage New York Avenue. I will end my turn and hold blockers without building or mortgaging.

p2 can mortgage their railroads, Park Place, and Boardwalk to raise about $740 in cash. That is enough to survive a light blue hotel hit. They are not about to hand the dark blue monopoly to p4 immediately.

Breaking the dark blue set is not urgent enough to sacrifice my survival buffer. p4 has $1752 and only needs Atlantic Avenue and Marvin Gardens to complete the yellow monopoly, so I must never sell Marvin. If I land on Atlantic, buying it would block p4 from completing yellow, but that is a landing decision rather than a post-turn action.

I cannot buy unowned properties except when landing. I considered trading with p4 for Virginia to complete the pink set, but that would require giving up Marvin or other pinks. Even then, three houses on the pink set cost $900, which is too expensive to build safely.

I will not reveal strategy in public messages. I will keep my post-turn action brief and simply end the turn.

I rejected offering Water Works plus Marvin to p2, since that would hand p4 the property they need. I am now considering a direct trade with p3: give them Water Works for about $120 cash. That would raise my cash buffer from $241 to $361 and improve my total liquidity.

The Water Works trade with p3 is rejected because it reveals a cash need and offers too little return. I am now examining mortgaged properties like North Carolina and Indiana as cheap acquisition targets, though p3 already holds Pacific and p4 owns Pennsylvania Avenue.

I will end my turn. I noted that I am in jail but not marked as in_jail, which is odd but not actionable.
